question: Which of these is NOT a core nursing responsibility for a patient on targeted receptor therapy?

options.A: Performing surgery to remove the endocrine glands
options.B: Providing emotional support for distressing physical side effects
options.C: Monitoring the patient closely for side effects related to hormone blockade
options.D: Educating the patient on the importance of taking medications regularly

explanation: Surgeons handle the operating room; nurses shine in assessment, patient education, emotional care, and managing side effects. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h7)

question: Why do patients with Alzheimer's slowly lose their memory and thinking skills?

options.A: Excess fluid builds up and creates pressure inside the skull
options.B: The brain temporarily stops producing enough blood and oxygen
options.C: Infections in the spinal cord destroy nerve pathways
options.D: Protein deposits cause brain cell damage and cell death

explanation: Exactly! Those protein plaques and tangles block cell communication, eventually leading to brain cell damage and shrinkage. Great clinical insight!

question: Why is building trust with the community so important for a nurse?

options.A: It legally protects the nurse from medical malpractice lawsuits
options.B: It encourages community members to accept immunizations and report illnesses early
options.C: It eliminates the need for any environmental sanitation work
options.D: It guarantees financial funding from international donors

explanation: Spot on! People are much more likely to listen, take their vaccines, and share health worries when they know and trust their nurse.

question: What is a key difference between the anterior and posterior pituitary lobes?

options.A: The anterior lobe releases oxytocin into the bloodstream.
options.B: The anterior lobe ignores signals from the hypothalamus.
options.C: The posterior lobe produces growth hormone directly.
options.D: The posterior lobe only stores hormones made by the hypothalamus.

explanation: Well done! Think of the posterior pituitary as a warehouse—it doesn't make oxytocin or ADH itself, it just stores and releases them.

question: Why are transparent procurement rules so important in public health?

options.A: To ensure that all drugs are manufactured inside government hospitals
options.B: To remove the need for any financial auditing
options.C: To prevent inflated contract costs and substandard medical supplies
options.D: To allow doctors to bypass the budgeting process

explanation: Strict procurement rules stop corrupt contractors from overpricing items or supplying fake and substandard drugs to hospitals.

question: Where do lipid-soluble hormones find their specific receptors?

options.A: Inside the cytoplasm or nucleus
options.B: Attached to the exterior of the blood vessel
options.C: Embedded in the outer cell membrane
options.D: Floating freely in the extracellular fluid

explanation: Lipid-soluble hormones easily cross membranes, so their receptors wait for them inside the cell or nucleus. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h4)

question: As a student nurse or midwife, what is a key way you can promote safe motherhood in your community?

options.A: Educating families on danger signs and encouraging hospital delivery
options.B: Paying the hospital transport bills for poor pregnant women personally
options.C: Performing major surgeries inside primary health centers without doctors
options.D: Making laws to punish traditional birth attendants who work in villages

explanation: Community health education saves lives! Teaching families what warning signs to look out for helps them get moms to the hospital before it's too late.

question: Wernicke encephalopathy is caused by a severe shortage of which vitamin?

options.A: Vitamin D
options.B: Vitamin B12
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin B1

explanation: Spot on! Wernicke encephalopathy happens specifically when the body lacks enough thiamine, which is Vitamin B1.

question: What is the main goal of 'active case finding' during an outbreak?

options.A: To conduct routine training for nursing students
options.B: To audit the financial accounts of the local hospital
options.C: To replace expired medications in the pharmacy store
options.D: To search for additional unrecorded cases in the community

explanation: Instead of waiting for sick people to walk into the clinic, active case finding means going out into the community to find anyone else who might be hiding or missing treatment.

question: Why is it important for the nurse to explain the rectal procedure thoroughly before beginning?

options.A: It guarantees that the drug will bypass liver metabolism
options.B: It replaces the need for wearing clean gloves during insertion
options.C: It helps reduce patient anxiety and embarrassment
options.D: It chemically speeds up the breakdown of the suppository base

explanation: The rectal procedure is sensitive and personal; clear communication builds trust and calms the patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h8)

question: Why should nurses separate the concepts of 'sex' and 'gender'?

options.A: It removes the need to collect demographic data during patient admission
options.B: It ensures that patients are only treated based on their chromosome count
options.C: It helps identify which health issues stem from biology versus societal rules
options.D: It proves that biological traits change more quickly than cultural norms

explanation: Separating them helps you see the whole picture. Some health problems happen because of our biology, while others happen because of society's rules and expectations for men and women.

question: Which of these is a macronutrient that our bodies need in large amounts?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Minerals
options.C: Water-soluble enzymes
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs, proteins, and fats are your macronutrients—the heavy lifters our bodies need in big quantities every day!

question: When is the best time to initiate breastfeeding after an uncomplicated delivery?

options.A: Within the first hour of birth
options.B: Once the milk transitions to white
options.C: After twenty-four hours of rest
options.D: After the baby receives initial vaccines

explanation: Starting breastfeeding within the first hour takes advantage of the baby's alert state and helps milk production start smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: A community nurse notices that pregnant women in a remote village have nowhere to go for antenatal care. What is the best action?

options.A: Tell the pregnant women to relocate permanently to the capital
options.B: Ignore the issue since hospitals are solely a government duty
options.C: Collaborate with a voluntary health agency to set up mobile clinics
options.D: Wait until the villagers independently build a standard hospital

explanation: Brilliant nursing judgment! Partnering with voluntary organizations is one of the smartest ways to bring care straight to underserved communities.

question: What is the main feature that separates chronic osteomyelitis from acute osteomyelitis?

options.A: The complete inability of bacteria to cause tissue damage
options.B: The duration of the infection lasting for months or years
options.C: The restriction of the disease to flat facial bones
options.D: The total absence of any pain or localized swelling

explanation: The big difference is time! Chronic means it has been hanging around stubbornly for months or even years.

question: Why does injecting local numbing medicine directly into the middle of an inflamed abscess often not work very well?

options.A: The acidic environment of the pus neutralizes the local anesthetic
options.B: The nerve endings in the center are already permanently destroyed
options.C: The pus pressure pushes the medication back out the needle hole
options.D: The thick skin blocks the numbing medicine from spreading

explanation: Infected, pus-filled areas have an acidic chemistry that stops the numbing medicine from doing its job. That is why doctors usually numb the healthy skin around the edges instead!

question: What score on the muscle strength grading scale indicates normal strength against full resistance?

options.A: Grade 10
options.B: Grade 1
options.C: Grade 3
options.D: Grade 5

explanation: A grade of 5 out of 5 is the standard score for normal muscle strength where the client easily overcomes resistance. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the main point of doing a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?

options.A: To measure the exact size of the patient's lung capacity
options.B: To clean out thick secretions from the lower airways
options.C: To give the mechanical ventilator a chance to rest and cool down
options.D: To test if the patient can breathe without full ventilator support

explanation: An SBT dials back the machine's help to see if the patient's own breathing muscles are ready to take over the job.

question: Which of these is NOT part of a holistic palliative assessment?

options.A: Respecting cultural beliefs and family traditions
options.B: Strictly monitoring laboratory blood cell counts
options.C: Evaluating emotional and psychological well-being
options.D: Listening to spiritual and existential concerns

explanation: While lab results matter in acute care, palliative care is all about the human experience—feelings, culture, and spirit. It's much more than just numbers on a lab sheet!

question: Why is economic stability so important when a community health nurse tries to lower disease rates?

options.A: Economic status is the only factor recorded on a hospital admission form
options.B: Government policies prevent nurses from treating poor patients
options.C: Poverty often limits access to clean water, good food, and proper sanitation
options.D: Wealthy neighborhoods never experience infectious disease outbreaks

explanation: Well reasoned! When people have a stable income, they can easily afford basic needs like safe water and good nutrition, which naturally keeps diseases away.

question: How many pulmonary veins normally return oxygenated blood to the heart?

options.A: One
options.B: Four
options.C: Two
options.D: Six

explanation: There are typically four pulmonary veins in total, with two coming from each lung. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of delivering a shock with an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)?

options.A: To warm up cold heart muscle tissue after a cardiac arrest
options.B: To interrupt a chaotic heart rhythm and let it reset
options.C: To measure the exact blood pressure inside the ventricles
options.D: To restart a completely flat heart line during asystole

explanation: Think of the AED as a reset button! It momentarily stuns a wildly quivering heart so the heart's natural pacemaker can take back control.

question: Which of these is a key community role for a nurse promoting safe motherhood?

options.A: Manufacturing routine pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Managing hospital financial budgets
options.C: Performing major obstetric surgeries alone
options.D: Health education and mobilizing families

explanation: You got it! Teaching families about danger signs and encouraging them to visit the clinic early is one of our best community tools.

question: Which of these is considered the most serious complication of an endoscopy?

options.A: Mild throat irritation from the tube
options.B: Perforation of the organ wall
options.C: Passing gas shortly after waking up
options.D: Temporary drowsiness from sedation

explanation: A tear (perforation) in the gut wall is a serious emergency because it can let bacteria leak into the body, requiring immediate medical care.

question: Why do health programs often fail when they are imposed from the outside without community involvement?

options.A: They fail to match cultural realities and local priorities
options.B: Governments never allow outsiders to visit villages
options.C: Local health workers refuse to touch foreign supplies
options.D: They always cost too much money to run

explanation: Interventions that ignore local values and real community needs lack ownership and fail to gain public trust. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which condition is a strict, absolute 'no-go' for giving radioactive iodine (I-131) therapy?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Advanced age
options.C: Mild tachycardia
options.D: Pregnancy

explanation: Radioactive iodine can cross the placenta and harm the baby's developing thyroid, so pregnancy is an absolute contraindication.

question: Long before modern labs, how did early humans figure out which foods were safe to eat?

options.A: Microscopic testing
options.B: Written government guidelines
options.C: Trial and error
options.D: Chemical analysis

explanation: Spot on! Before science labs, our ancestors had to rely on simple observation and trying things out to see what was safe to put in their bodies.

question: How does a cold compress help reduce pain?

options.A: By increasing the local metabolic rate of damaged cells
options.B: By slowing down nerve conduction velocity to numb the site
options.C: By permanently destroying local sensory pain receptors
options.D: By flushing out inflammatory toxins through massive vasodilation

explanation: Cold temperatures slow down how fast nerve signals travel, acting like a natural, gentle local anesthetic for the skin.

question: A patient with severe liver failure will most likely have trouble with which normal body process?

options.A: Pumping blood to the brain
options.B: Detoxifying chemicals in the blood
options.C: Filtering red blood cells out of urine
options.D: Exchanging oxygen in the alveoli

explanation: Great job! One of the liver's main jobs is to break down and filter toxins and medications from your bloodstream.

question: Which of these options is NOT a workplace hazard that threatens reproductive health?

options.A: Working around sources of ionizing radiation
options.B: Handling organic solvents in factories
options.C: Daily consumption of pasteurized milk
options.D: Prolonged exposure to heavy metals like lead

explanation: Easy peasy! Pasteurized milk is a healthy drink, not a toxic workplace chemical. Keep flying through these questions—you've got this!

question: Why is sudden, unexplained weight loss a big warning sign in digestive health?

options.A: It means the patient is simply exercising too much
options.B: It shows that digestion is working much faster than normal
options.C: It often points to chronic malabsorption or underlying disease
options.D: It is a harmless change that happens as people age

explanation: When the gut struggles to absorb nutrients, or an illness burns through energy, the body weight drops quickly. It's an important clue for nurses!

question: What do we call the tiny gaps found between the insulated segments of myelin along an axon?

options.A: Axon hillocks
options.B: Nodes of Ranvier
options.C: Nissl bodies
options.D: Synaptic clefts

explanation: The nodes of Ranvier are the bare spots between myelin wraps where electrical signals get a quick boost to travel faster.

question: A young girl who recently underwent FGM refuses to urinate, looks restless, and has a swollen lower abdomen. What is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: Bowel obstruction
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Acute urinary retention

explanation: Well done! Severe pain, swelling, and fear often cause girls to hold their urine, leading to a painfully full bladder and acute urinary retention.

question: What is the primary function of a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: To record electrical impulses passing through the heart muscle
options.C: To check how well the kidneys filter waste products from urine
options.D: To detect the genetic material of a virus or bacterium

explanation: PCR tests amplify small amounts of DNA or RNA to confirm the exact presence of the infectious agent. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h6)

question: What can happen if you use the wrong liquid (diluent) to mix a vaccine?

options.A: It can destroy the vaccine or harm the client
options.B: It doubles the number of active doses inside the vial
options.C: It automatically turns the liquid into a bright blue color
options.D: It extends the expiration date by exactly six months

explanation: Every vaccine has a specific liquid made just for it. Using the wrong one ruins the dose and compromises patient safety.

question: Why does the surface of the brain have so many folds and grooves?

options.A: To improve the circulation of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: To increase the surface area for more neurons
options.C: To separate the left and right sides of the body
options.D: To absorb physical shock from head injuries

explanation: Folding packs a massive amount of brain power into a small space, giving us room for lots of nerve cells!

question: Which body area absorbs topical medications the fastest, often requiring a lower concentration?

options.A: The face and skin folds
options.B: The soles of the feet
options.C: The palms of the hands
options.D: The thick skin of the back

explanation: Thin skin areas absorb medications much quicker, increasing the risk of irritation if the drug is too strong. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h2)

question: Why can suddenly stopping long-term steroid medications trigger an adrenal crisis?

options.A: Stopping steroids causes the liver to destroy all circulating glucose
options.B: Steroid pills turn into toxic acid inside the stomach lining
options.C: The adrenal glands become lazy and stop making natural cortisol
options.D: The thyroid gland reacts by shutting down body temperature controls

explanation: When you take external steroids for a long time, your adrenals take a break from making their own. If you stop abruptly, they can't bounce back fast enough!

question: How long should patients wait at the clinic after getting an immunization?

options.A: At least 15 minutes
options.B: Exactly two hours
options.C: Until the end of the market day
options.D: No waiting time is required

explanation: That 15-minute window is a crucial safety check just in case a rare allergic reaction pops up right away.

question: Why might a traumatized patient complain of chest tightness and nausea even when all their medical tests are normal?

options.A: The patient is intentionally trying to fake their injuries
options.B: A delayed infection is spreading through the bloodstream
options.C: Somatization translates emotional stress into physical symptoms
options.D: Standard hospital diagnostic machines are malfunctioning

explanation: Exactly! The mind and body are deeply connected. Emotional distress can show up as very real physical feelings like upset stomachs or tight chests—this is called somatization.

question: Why is eating or drinking inside a chemical storage room a major safety violation?

options.A: It creates a direct pathway for hand-to-mouth chemical ingestion
options.B: It attracts pests that chew through the chemical packaging
options.C: Digestion slows down significantly in cold storage rooms
options.D: Food particles will ruin the chemical composition of stored products

explanation: Exactly right! Invisible chemical residues can settle on your hands, food, or drinks, making it super easy to swallow them by accident. Always keep food and drinks well away from chemicals!

question: What is the main benefit of using hydrotherapy (water exercise) in rehab?

options.A: Water buoyancy reduces joint stress during physical exercise.
options.B: It replaces the need for any nutritional support.
options.C: It eliminates all risks of secondary skin infections.
options.D: It completely cures chronic neurological disorders in days.

explanation: Well done! The water helps support the patient's weight, taking pressure off painful or weak joints so they can move more easily.

question: What is the main nutritional catch of relying on just one single staple food, like only eating cassava for every meal?

options.A: It provides zero calories needed for daily physical activity
options.B: It lacks a complete profile of essential proteins and fats
options.C: It causes immediate and severe vitamin toxicity in adults
options.D: It contains too much dietary fiber for the human stomach

explanation: Spot on! While staples give great energy, eating only one thing leaves big gaps in other vital nutrients. Variety is always key!

question: What is the most serious, life-threatening side effect nurses must watch out for when giving opioids?

options.A: Severe muscle cramping
options.B: Respiratory depression
options.C: Rapid hair loss
options.D: Sudden high blood pressure

explanation: You've got this! Opioids slow down the brain's breathing center, which is why checking the patient's respiratory rate is a vital nursing duty.

question: What does it mean if a symptom shows up long after the normal incubation window has passed?

options.A: The patient's immune system is too perfect
options.B: The disease has been totally cured by magic
options.C: The laboratory test results are always wrong
options.D: It points to a different sickness or a newer exposure

explanation: When the timeline doesn't fit standard patterns, nurses should suspect a different illness or that the patient picked up the bug a second time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h4)

question: What is the minimum head-of-bed elevation for a patient on continuous tube feeding?

options.A: 30 to 45 degrees
options.B: 10 to 15 degrees
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: 60 to 90 degrees

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the head of the bed raised prevents the formula from flowing backward into the lungs.

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient taking a 7-day course of antibiotics for cervicitis?

options.A: Share the remaining pills with your partner to save money.
options.B: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill.
options.C: Stop taking the pills immediately if mild stomach upset occurs.
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better early.

explanation: Always remind patients to complete their full dose! Stopping early can cause the infection to bounce back stronger.

question: Why is a fever in a neutropenic patient considered a medical emergency?

options.A: It causes severe bleeding that is impossible to stop
options.B: A compromised immune system means a mild infection can rapidly turn fatal
options.C: It always causes permanent paralysis in the legs
options.D: It instantly stops the kidneys from producing any urine

explanation: Without enough white blood cells to fight back, a small fever can quickly become overwhelming. Quick action with antibiotics saves lives here!

question: Why is meal timing just as important as food choice for a patient taking insulin?

options.A: Consistent meal timing prevents dangerous mismatches with peak medication action.
options.B: Insulin can only digest food if it is eaten exactly at sunrise.
options.C: Skipping meals causes insulin to turn directly into body fat.
options.D: Late meals make the pancreas stop working permanently.

explanation: When insulin is active in the body without food present, blood sugar can drop to dangerously low levels. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h1)

question: If a patient has joint pain along with skin rashes and unusual sensitivity to sunlight, what systemic condition might they have?

options.A: Primary osteoarthritis
options.B: Systemic lupus erythematosus
options.C: Acute bone fracture
options.D: Simple muscle strain

explanation: Spot-on! Lupus is an autoimmune disease famous for causing joint pain alongside a butterfly-shaped face rash and sun sensitivity.

question: What naturally happens to a pregnant woman's blood (plasma) volume during normal gestation?

options.A: It increases significantly
options.B: It remains completely unchanged
options.C: It decreases by half
options.D: It drops to zero temporarily

explanation: Plasma volume expands greatly during pregnancy to supply the placenta and keep up with the body's new demands. Amazing how the body adapts!

question: How does the lymphatic system primarily support the cardiovascular system?

options.A: By regulating the overall resting blood pressure
options.B: By returning leaked interstitial fluid back to the bloodstream
options.C: By pumping oxygenated blood directly to body tissues
options.D: By producing red blood cells to replace old ones

explanation: Fluid constantly escapes blood capillaries into tissues, and the lymphatic system collects and returns this fluid to maintain circulation volume. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: What do we call the process where cancer cells break away and spread through the blood or lymph to other parts of the body?

options.A: Mitosis
options.B: Metastasis
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Apoptosis

explanation: You're doing great! Metastasis happens when malignant cells travel via blood or lymph to set up secondary growths in distant organs.

question: A patient's joint fluid report mentions hemarthrosis. What does this mean?

options.A: Normal wear and tear from aging
options.B: A severe bacterial infection in the joint
options.C: An advanced stage of rheumatoid arthritis
options.D: Recent trauma or bleeding inside the joint

explanation: Hemarthrosis simply means there is blood inside the joint space. You will usually see this after a physical injury, a heavy fall, or recent joint surgery.

question: Why should nurses use a friendly, non-judgmental tone when asking patients about drug use?

options.A: It legally protects the nurse from malpractice suits
options.B: It encourages patients to provide honest health disclosures
options.C: It ensures the doctor prescribes higher drug doses
options.D: It prevents the patient from staying in the hospital

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from moral blame, they are much more honest about their health history. Great nursing care starts with empathy!

question: A patient with severe fatigue insists on cleaning their whole house in one go, leaving them bedridden for days afterward. What nursing advice should you give?

options.A: Avoid all movement for the next month to let muscles heal.
options.B: Break chores into small parts and rest between each task.
options.C: Increase caffeine intake to maintain speed through the cleaning.
options.D: Perform all cleaning tasks immediately after waking up.

explanation: You're learning great clinical judgment! Splitting big tasks into smaller chunks and resting in between helps patients break the exhausting 'boom-and-bust' cycle.

question: A newly bereaved family member sits quietly without crying and says everything is fine. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The person is lying to trick the medical staff
options.B: The person lacks any emotional capacity for love
options.C: The person may be experiencing shock or emotional numbing
options.D: The person has already successfully reached full acceptance

explanation: A lack of tears does not always mean peace; it often indicates emotional shock or denial. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why should a home health nurse check the patient's skin while helping them take a bath?

options.A: To spot early signs of skin breakdown and pressure injuries
options.B: To apply strong chemical disinfectants to normal dry skin
options.C: To measure the exact body temperature of the skin surface
options.D: To determine if the patient has applied expensive lotion

explanation: Brilliant! Bath time is prime time for assessment. It gives you a great chance to look at hard-to-see spots like the back, elbows, and heels for early redness or pressure sores.

question: Which of the following is an example of an open-ended question?

options.A: Are you finished having children with your husband?
options.B: Do you want to use pills or injections today?
options.C: What worries you most about using family planning methods?
options.D: Have you ever experienced high blood pressure before?

explanation: This question cannot be answered with a simple yes or no, prompting the client to elaborate on their specific fears. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: Who do state-level anti-FGM laws mostly target for arrest?

options.A: Traditional cutters who perform the procedure
options.B: Local pharmacists selling basic antibiotics
options.C: Mothers who miss child vaccination appointments
options.D: Traditional birth attendants helping with normal deliveries

explanation: Spot on! State laws specifically target the individuals who physically perform the cutting, as well as those who actively sponsor or demand it.

question: A 28-week pregnant client comes in complaining of a pounding headache and sudden blurry vision. What should pop into your head first?

options.A: A simple reaction to eating too much sugar
options.B: Signs of potential pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Normal physiological changes due to increased sleep
options.D: Standard fatigue that requires drinking more coffee

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision combined in pregnancy are classic red flags for pre-eclampsia. Grab that BP cuff right away!

question: What is a vital nursing action when feeding a patient who has trouble swallowing?

options.A: Avoid checking the mouth after meals
options.B: Provide only large dry food portions
options.C: Keep the patient in an upright position
options.D: Encourage the patient to lie flat quickly

explanation: Gravity is your best friend here! Keeping your patient upright helps food travel down safely and protects their lungs from accidental choking or aspiration.

question: Why is sudden, heavy postpartum bleeding that causes dizziness treated as a top emergency?

options.A: It prevents the mother from producing enough breast milk
options.B: It quickly leads to hypovolemic shock and organ failure
options.C: It always results in permanent damage to the kidneys
options.D: It causes the baby to reject breastfeeding due to stress

explanation: Rapid blood loss starves vital organs of oxygen. Without fast intervention, the mother's body can slip into shock very quickly.

question: Why must the ear pinna be pulled downward and backward for a child under three years old?

options.A: The eardrum sits at a completely different angle in infants
options.B: It prevents the child from turning their head sideways
options.C: Children have more earwax blocking the upper canal
options.D: Their ear canal is shorter and straighter compared to an adult

explanation: An infant's ear canal anatomy requires a downward and backward pull to properly align the passage for drops. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h2)

question: A patient with advanced dementia makes a pain face, holds their tummy, and has a fast heart rate, but says they have no pain. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient because they cannot feel pain.
options.B: Ignore the physical signs since the verbal denial overrides them.
options.C: Treat these non-verbal behavioral signs as reliable indicators of pain.
options.D: Wait until the patient is able to provide a clear numeric score.

explanation: When dementia makes talking difficult, body language tells the real story. Trust those physical cues!

question: Why do patients who recover from a severe kidney injury need long-term blood pressure checks?

options.A: Kidney damage can disrupt blood flow regulation and trigger chronic hypertension.
options.B: Blood pressure medication prevents the formation of scar tissue in the ureter.
options.C: High blood pressure is the primary cause of external genital trauma.
options.D: Kidney injuries always cause permanent low blood pressure due to fluid loss.

explanation: Our kidneys help control our blood pressure. If scarring messes up their hormone signals, it can lead to long-term high blood pressure down the road.

question: What action should a nurse take when a fiberglass measuring tape starts to show stretched markings?

options.A: Use a pen to redraw the faded numbers
options.B: Pull it tighter to compensate for the stretch
options.C: Discard and replace it immediately
options.D: Only use it for adult patients instead of children

explanation: Once a tape loses its calibration through stretching, it can no longer provide trustworthy clinical measurements. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why can severe physical stress or a sudden infection cause a high fasting blood sugar reading?

options.A: Infection causes the kidneys to stop filtering sugar out of the blood.
options.B: Dehydration turns blood cells into pure glucose molecules.
options.C: Fever completely destroys insulin molecules stored in the pancreas.
options.D: Stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline are released, raising blood glucose.

explanation: You've got this! Acute stress triggers your body to release hormones that push stored glucose into the bloodstream to give you energy for a fight-or-flight response.

question: What is the main goal of the DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy Short-Course) program?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of manufacturing TB drugs
options.B: To eliminate the need for sputum microscopy tests
options.C: To force patients to stay admitted in the hospital for six months
options.D: To ensure patients swallow every dose of medicine to prevent drug resistance

explanation: With DOTS, a health worker watches the patient take their medication. This makes sure they finish the course and stops drug-resistant TB from developing.

question: What is the classic sign that patients usually report when they have a bone tumor?

options.A: Itchy skin rashes directly over the affected joint
options.B: Sudden numbness and tingling in the toes of both feet
options.C: Persistent, worsening bone pain that is often present at night
options.D: Sharp shooting pain that only happens during heavy physical exercise

explanation: Unlike normal muscle aches, bone tumor pain is relentless, gets worse over time, and loves to wake patients up at night.

question: A patient comes to the clinic struggling with a weak urine stream after a past pelvic injury. What procedure are they most likely getting ready for?

options.A: Gastric tube insertion
options.B: Urethral dilation
options.C: Endotracheal intubation
options.D: Esophageal manometry

explanation: Pelvic trauma can cause scarring in the urethra (the urine passage), leading to a tight spot or stricture that needs to be gently stretched out to restore normal flow.

question: What is the true foundation of evidence-based practice in nursing?

options.A: Following the personal opinions of senior administrative staff
options.B: Using the cheapest medical supplies available on the market
options.C: Strict adherence to traditional hospital routines
options.D: Combining best research evidence with clinical expertise and patient values

explanation: You've got it! Evidence-based practice is a sweet spot: it blends what science proves works, your clinical skills as a nurse, and what the patient actually wants. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h4)

question: To be most effective after an unprotected sexual assault, within how many hours should emergency contraception be given?

options.A: 120 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: 12 hours
options.D: 48 hours

explanation: Well remembered! Emergency contraceptive pills work best when taken within 120 hours (or 5 days) after exposure.

question: What is the main goal of doing a situation analysis in community health nursing?

options.A: To gather comprehensive data about population health and resources
options.B: To punish local leaders for failing to meet health targets
options.C: To replace traditional healers with western medical doctors
options.D: To enforce strict government regulations on local businesses

explanation: Spot on! Before planning any care, you need to understand the community's actual health status and available resources so your efforts hit the mark.

question: What is the main sign of acute urinary retention?

options.A: Slow, painless loss of small amounts of urine all day
options.B: Sudden and painful inability to pass urine
options.C: Total absence of urine production by the kidneys
options.D: Constant burning pain while urinating frequently

explanation: Acute retention happens quickly and hurts a lot because the bladder fills up fast and cannot empty. You've got this!

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of a localized infection following suture removal?

options.A: Mild itching around the adhesive strips
options.B: Temporary skin numbness near the cut
options.C: Pus drainage and spreading skin warmth
options.D: Fading pink color of the scar line

explanation: Pus and warmth indicate bacterial multiplication and active inflammation, which signal that the wound is becoming infected. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is often the earliest sign that the brain isn't getting enough blood in a heart patient?

options.A: Inability to move the tongue
options.B: A sudden change in mental status or confusion
options.C: Yellow skin color
options.D: Pain in the big toe

explanation: The brain is a drama queen when it comes to oxygen—it complains immediately! Mild confusion or restlessness is usually the very first red flag that circulation is failing.

question: A patient is physically stable after recovering from an intentional overdose. What is the most important next step in their care?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a warning never to return
options.B: Scold the patient for wasting hospital resources and staff time
options.C: Arrange for a mental health evaluation and ongoing psychological support
options.D: Assume the underlying issue is resolved and stop all observation

explanation: Physical healing is only half the battle. For intentional self-harm, a psychiatric assessment and emotional support before discharge are essential for keeping the patient safe.

question: Which strategy is most effective when educating rural community members about pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: Using simple local dialects and relatable community gathering spaces
options.B: Hosting lectures exclusively in urban tertiary teaching hospitals
options.C: Requiring written exams before women can attend antenatal care
options.D: Distributing dense medical journals written in advanced technical terms

explanation: Effective community health education meets people where they are, using familiar language and local venues like markets or places of worship. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h5)

question: A patient using axillary crutches complains of numbness and tingling in their fingers. What instruction should the nurse provide?

options.A: Switch immediately to using a standard four-wheeled walker
options.B: Adjust the crutches so they fit higher up in the armpit
options.C: Lean your upper body forward to relieve hand pressure
options.D: Support your body weight on your hands, not your armpits

explanation: Resting body weight on the armpits compresses nerves and blood vessels, leading to nerve damage and tingling; weight must go through the hand grips. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h4)

question: What is the main job of a skilled birth attendant during a home delivery?

options.A: To transport the mother to a hospital for every contraction
options.B: To prescribe long-term contraception before labor starts
options.C: To perform emergency cesarean sections in the home
options.D: To monitor mother and baby and manage normal childbirth

explanation: You've got this! A skilled birth attendant is simply there to watch how labor progresses, support the mother, and safely handle a normal delivery while keeping an eye out for any trouble.

question: Which medication class is widely known to cause constipation as a side effect?

options.A: Short-acting diuretics
options.B: Opioid pain relievers
options.C: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.D: Broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Opioids slow down gastrointestinal motility significantly, which frequently leads to stubborn constipation in patients taking them. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why is quarantine used as a public health tool during an outbreak?

options.A: To stop exposed people from spreading the disease further
options.B: To cure people who already have the infection
options.C: To punish individuals who travel without permission
options.D: To test new vaccines on healthy populations

explanation: Restricting movement of exposed persons prevents them from passing germs to the community during the incubation period. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h1)

question: A patient scheduled for surgery takes daily aspirin for joint pain. What is your main concern as their nurse?

options.A: Aspirin causes a dangerous spike in white blood cell counts
options.B: Aspirin inhibits platelet function and can cause excessive bleeding
options.C: Aspirin turns the patient's blood bright green in the tubing
options.D: Aspirin completely stops the kidneys from producing urine

explanation: Aspirin stops platelets from sticking together properly. Before surgery, this puts the patient at high risk for heavy bleeding.

question: A patient has patchy hair loss and scalp tenderness from wearing tight braids for months. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Pediculosis capitis
options.B: Alopecia areata
options.C: Traction alopecia
options.D: Seborrheic dermatitis

explanation: Constant pulling on the hair roots from tight hairstyles damages them over time, leading to hair loss known as traction alopecia. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: What happens during the T wave of a normal heartbeat?

options.A: The main heart valves snap shut to trap blood inside
options.B: The electrical signal fires off inside the sinus node
options.C: Blood rushes rapidly from the body into the right atrium
options.D: The ventricles recharge and get ready for the next beat

explanation: The T wave marks ventricular repolarization, which is the electrical recovery or resting state of the lower chambers. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main difference between shear and friction in skin breakdown?

options.A: Shear only happens on the heels, whereas friction only happens on the sacrum.
options.B: Shear happens when bones slide inside while skin stays stuck; friction is just surface rubbing.
options.C: Shear damages bone tissue, whereas friction only damages hair follicles.
options.D: Shear is caused by moisture, whereas friction is caused by lack of protein.

explanation: Friction is like skin rubbing against bedsheets, but shear happens when the skeleton slides down while the outer skin stays put, twisting the blood vessels inside. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal mortality?

options.A: Benign breast lumps
options.B: Chronic dental caries
options.C: Uncomplicated malaria
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after childbirth is one of the top direct causes of maternal death worldwide. Knowing how to spot and manage it is essential for every nursing student!

question: A nurse in a rural Nigerian clinic notices more waterborne diseases during the rainy season. What action best reflects PHC philosophy?

options.A: Wait inside the clinic and only treat patients who manage to walk in with severe diarrhea
options.B: Collaborate with community leaders to organize safe water education and promote simple water boiling methods
options.C: Complain to the federal government and refuse to see any more sick patients
options.D: Refer every single patient immediately to a foreign overseas hospital

explanation: Spot on! Being proactive with education and community teamwork stops outbreaks at the grassroots before they overwhelm the clinic.

question: What does your body do with extra carbohydrates when you eat more than you immediately need?

options.A: It converts all excess carbohydrates directly into bone tissue.
options.B: It eliminates them completely through the urinary system.
options.C: It stores the extra fuel as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
options.D: It turns them into water molecules to hydrate the cells.

explanation: Nothing goes to waste! When you have extra energy, your body packs it away neatly as glycogen in your liver and muscles for later use.

question: A recovering heart patient is ready to take their first walk down the ward corridor. What should you do?

options.A: Attach a portable telemetry or wireless monitoring unit
options.B: Keep the patient attached to a heavy wall-mounted monitor with long cables
options.C: Wait until the patient returns to the bed to check vitals
options.D: Disconnect all monitoring devices to encourage normal movement

explanation: Early walks are great for recovery, but we always want a wireless or telemetry unit attached so we can safely watch out for any exercise-related heart issues.

question: Which of the following is a common home hazard that frequently leads to patient falls?

options.A: Bright lighting in bedroom hallways
options.B: Grab bars installed inside showers
options.C: Low-pile wall-to-wall carpeting
options.D: Loose scatter rugs on slick floors

explanation: Loose rugs easily slip underfoot or catch assistive device tips, making them a major tripping hazard in homes. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is pharmacovigilance?

options.A: The clinical trial phase testing drugs on healthy animal subjects
options.B: The mathematical calculation of correct pediatric drug dosages
options.C: The monitoring and prevention of adverse drug reactions
options.D: The process of manufacturing cheap generic pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Pharmacovigilance centers on detecting and tracking adverse drug events to ensure ongoing medication safety. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h6)

question: A patient says quitting is pointless because their health is already ruined. Which 'R' should the nurse use first to motivate them?

options.A: Relevance
options.B: Rewards
options.C: Repetition
options.D: Readiness

explanation: Connecting quitting directly to their personal health situation makes the conversation meaningful to them. Excellent clinical reasoning!

question: Which lab test is most commonly used to find Chlamydia and Gonorrhea in men quickly and accurately?

options.A: Complete Blood Count with differential
options.B: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
options.C: Basic metabolic electrolyte panel
options.D: Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT)

explanation: NAAT is the gold standard! It's super sensitive and can even be done using a simple urine sample.

question: Which accessory gland makes the biggest chunk of the fluid found in semen?

options.A: Prostate gland
options.B: Seminal vesicles
options.C: Bulbourethral gland
options.D: Cowper's gland

explanation: The seminal vesicles are great providers—they supply the bulk of the fluid volume, including sweet sugars to give the sperm energy.

question: How does cigarette smoking increase the risk of developing vulval tumours?

options.A: It directly increases the production of estrogen in fatty tissues
options.B: It prevents the absorption of key vitamins needed for skin health
options.C: It impairs local immunity and works with HPV to promote cell changes
options.D: It causes immediate physical trauma to the external genitalia

explanation: Correct! Smoking weakens the body's local immune response, making it harder to fight off infections like HPV that trigger bad cell changes.

question: What is the primary goal of pharmacovigilance in healthcare?

options.A: To monitor and detect adverse drug reactions to ensure patient safety
options.B: To calculate the wholesale manufacturing cost of generic drugs
options.C: To supervise the physical packaging of pills in pharmacies
options.D: To market new pharmaceutical products to international hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Pharmacovigilance is all about watching out for bad drug reactions to keep patients safe.

question: What type of germ is Salmonella?

options.A: A bacterium
options.B: A fungus
options.C: A parasite
options.D: A virus

explanation: You got it! Salmonella is a single-celled bacterium that loves to multiply quickly when conditions are just right.

question: How are food nutrients mainly grouped based on how much the body needs them?

options.A: Macronutrients and micronutrients
options.B: Simple sugars and complex structures
options.C: Soluble and insoluble compounds
options.D: Animal-based and plant-based elements

explanation: We group them by quantity! 'Macro' means large (like carbs and proteins we need in bulk), and 'micro' means small (like vitamins needed in tiny amounts). Easy peasy!

question: Why should nurses avoid heavy medical jargon when explaining things to patients?

options.A: It causes patients to doubt the nurse's clinical training
options.B: It confuses patients and hinders their understanding of home care
options.C: It takes too much time to pronounce difficult words
options.D: It is considered unprofessional by hospital administrators

explanation: You nailed it. Plain, simple language helps patients truly grasp their care without feeling overwhelmed.

question: What vital sign must you watch most carefully after giving an IV opioid?

options.A: Oxygen saturation only
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Capillary refill
options.D: Body temperature

explanation: Safety first! Opioids can slow down the brain's breathing center, making your respiratory check the most important assessment in the room.

question: Why is it important for healthcare workers to understand the basic economics of food pricing?

options.A: It prevents nurses from ever having to worry about patient dietary budgets
options.B: It allows clinics to set direct retail prices for medications and supplies
options.C: It explains how economic shifts directly impact household nutrition and health outcomes
options.D: It qualifies nurses to manage local agricultural farms and crop yields

explanation: Understanding financial pressures helps clinicians recognize why patients might struggle to afford healthy diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h1)

question: What is the main job of Type A intercalated cells in the collecting duct?

options.A: Filtering water out of the blood plasma via high pressure
options.B: Reabsorbing large amounts of glucose into the blood
options.C: Secreting excess bicarbonate when blood is too alkaline
options.D: Secreting hydrogen ions into the urine during acidosis

explanation: When your body gets too acidic, Type A intercalated cells step up to pump extra hydrogen ions straight into the urine to help clear out the acid.

question: Why should Nigerian nurses do health education in the community alongside bedside care?

options.A: To fulfill strict legal requirements set by international bodies
options.B: To help demystify cultural myths and educate people on safe reproductive practices
options.C: To replace doctors during hospital strikes and emergencies
options.D: To generate extra revenue for the hospital administration

explanation: Great nurses know healing happens outside the ward too! Community talks help clear up dangerous myths and guide people toward safe practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which complication is best prevented by turning an immobile patient every two hours?

options.A: Pressure ulcers
options.B: Orthostatic hypotension
options.C: Foot drop contractures
options.D: Muscle atrophy

explanation: Moving patients regularly takes the weight off bony areas, giving the skin a chance to breathe and preventing painful bedsores.

question: What term describes physical traits like facial hair and breast development that are not direct reproductive organs?

options.A: Secondary sexual characteristics
options.B: Autonomic reflexes
options.C: Metabolic anomalies
options.D: Primary genetic markers

explanation: Spot on! Secondary sexual characteristics are those wonderful outward changes brought on by sex hormones that help distinguish the sexes.

question: Why do resource-limited regions often report higher rates of patient harm?

options.A: Local doctors have less formal education than foreign doctors
options.B: Medical technology in these regions is too advanced to operate
options.C: Weak infrastructure and understaffed facilities hinder safe care
options.D: Patients in these areas refuse to take their prescribed drugs

explanation: When hospitals lack steady power, enough staff, or basic supplies, it becomes much easier for errors to slip through.

question: How is Family Life Education different from clinical therapy?

options.A: Education requires a medical doctor license whereas therapy does not
options.B: Education is only practiced inside hospitals while therapy is done in schools
options.C: Education focuses on prevention and growth while therapy often focuses on remediation
options.D: Education deals exclusively with infants while therapy is for the elderly

explanation: You got it! Think of education as building strong life skills early, while therapy steps in later to help heal and fix existing emotional or relationship struggles.

question: Why do rehabilitation nursing goals need to be specific and measurable?

options.A: To ensure that all patients achieve the exact same recovery speed
options.B: To satisfy legal requirements for hospital discharge paperwork
options.C: To clearly track patient progress and know when goals are met
options.D: To prevent the patient from participating in care planning

explanation: Clear goals let the whole healthcare team see if the patient is improving and if the nursing care plan is working well.

question: What is the primary focus of medical services for special children?

options.A: Providing routine immunizations for infants
options.B: Meeting the unique developmental and physical needs of children with disabilities
options.C: Managing surgical emergencies in school-aged children
options.D: Treating only acute infectious diseases in hospitals

explanation: These specialized services focus on children who require extra medical, physical, or developmental support beyond standard care. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h1)

question: In simple terms, what does endocrine 'hyposecretion' mean?

options.A: Hormones are destroyed in the bloodstream
options.B: A gland produces too little of a hormone
options.C: A gland produces too much of a hormone
options.D: Target organs completely reject hormones

explanation: You've got this! 'Hypo-' always means under or low. So hyposecretion just means the gland isn't making enough hormone.

question: Which part of the brainstem contains the centers that control your heart rate and breathing?

options.A: Midbrain
options.B: Corpus callosum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The medulla oblongata keeps you alive by automatically running vital functions like your heartbeat and breathing rhythm.

question: Which equipment design helps lower the chance of a spinal headache?

options.A: Atraumatic pencil-point needles
options.B: Wide-bore metal needles
options.C: Disposable plastic syringes
options.D: Flexible silicone tubing

explanation: Correct! Pencil-point needles gently push fibers aside instead of cutting them, allowing the puncture hole to seal much faster.

question: How does family planning directly improve infant survival rates?

options.A: By eliminating childhood vaccinations completely
options.B: By replacing breast milk with specialized formula from birth
options.C: By guaranteeing that every child is born via cesarean section
options.D: By reducing the rate of premature births and low birth weight

explanation: Adequate birth spacing gives the uterus optimal conditions, resulting in healthier birth weights and fewer premature deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h2)

question: When a researcher is doing a quantitative study, what are they mainly looking at?

options.A: Audio recordings of patient interviews
options.B: Personal stories and emotional narratives
options.C: Numerical data and statistical analysis
options.D: Historical documents and old textbooks

explanation: You got it! Quantitative research is all about the numbers, measurements, and stats. Think 'Quantity = Numbers'! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which of these is considered an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?

options.A: Bathing and dressing
options.B: Balancing a checkbook
options.C: Shopping for groceries
options.D: Driving a motor vehicle

explanation: You nailed it! ADLs are the basic self-care tasks we do every day—like bathing, dressing, eating, and moving around. Simple and fundamental!

question: What is the main goal of environmental hygiene in public health?

options.A: Curing chronic illnesses using modern hospital equipment
options.B: Preventing diseases by controlling harmful environmental factors
options.C: Improving agricultural crop production and food storage
options.D: Increasing the economic wealth of local communities

explanation: You've got this! Environmental hygiene simply means managing our surroundings so that germs and hazards don't make people sick in the first place.

question: What is the main goal of hormone therapy in certain cancers?

options.A: To permanently increase the patient's natural testosterone and estrogen levels
options.B: To block or lower hormone levels that stimulate the growth of hormone-sensitive tumors
options.C: To completely replace failing endocrine glands throughout the entire body
options.D: To stimulate rapid production of red blood cells to prevent severe anemia

explanation: Exactly! Some cancers love hormones to grow. Hormone therapy cuts off that fuel supply to slow them down.

question: What is the main goal of tracking diseases closely (active surveillance) during an outbreak?

options.A: To replace traditional hospital admission procedures
options.B: To manufacture vaccines in community health centers
options.C: To track illness clusters and anticipate patient surges
options.D: To punish individuals who break quarantine rules

explanation: You got it! Surveillance helps us spot infection trends early and make sure hospitals are ready for incoming patients.

question: Who is primarily protected by the proper use of UN-certified transport packaging?

options.A: Hospital administrators managing the facility budget
options.B: Healthcare workers, couriers, and the general public
options.C: Patient family members waiting in the clinic lobby
options.D: Only the laboratory technicians performing the final analysis

explanation: Dangerous goods transit involves many handlers outside the hospital walls, making spill prevention vital for community health and safety. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: Which type of transmission happens when tiny germ particles float in the air over long distances?

options.A: Airborne transmission
options.B: Droplet transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Contact transmission

explanation: Airborne germs are lightweight and travel far on air currents, unlike heavier droplets that fall quickly.

question: What is the main medication used to treat General Paralysis of the Insane?

options.A: Corticosteroid shots
options.B: Intravenous Penicillin G
options.C: Oral antiviral tablets
options.D: Insulin injections

explanation: Well done! High-dose intravenous penicillin G is our top weapon to clear the Treponema pallidum bacteria out of the central nervous system.

question: Why is it important to teach patients how to navigate parties, weddings, and restaurants during dietary counselling?

options.A: It prevents the patient from ever eating junk food again
options.B: It proves that the nurse knows more than the patient
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will lose weight in one week
options.D: Real life includes parties and restaurants where strict rules do not fit

explanation: Brilliant thinking! Life is full of celebrations and social gatherings. Teaching flexible problem-solving helps patients stay healthy without missing out on the joy of living.

question: Which drug tragedy in the 1950s and 1960s caused severe birth defects and completely changed global drug safety rules?

options.A: Sulfanilamide
options.B: Thalidomide
options.C: Penicillin
options.D: Paracetamol

explanation: Spot on! Thalidomide was prescribed for morning sickness back then, but it sadly caused severe limb defects in babies, forcing the world to tighten up drug safety laws.

question: What does the 'teach-back' method mean when teaching a patient?

options.A: Giving the patient a written textbook to read silently
options.B: Testing the patient with a written multiple-choice exam
options.C: Asking the patient to repeat instructions in their own words
options.D: Demonstrating a procedure without speaking a single word

explanation: You nailed it! Teach-back is a simple way to confirm the patient truly understood what you explained.

question: Why do many people in local communities prefer getting injections from informal medicine shops?

options.A: Oral medications are completely unavailable in cities
options.B: Government policy requires informal shops to give shots
options.C: They believe injections work much faster than pills
options.D: Injections are always cheaper than tablets

explanation: It's a common belief that shooting medicine straight into the body heals you faster than swallowing a pill. As nurses, patient education on safe administration is key here!

question: What is the biggest advantage of school management partnering with local health authorities?

options.A: Free commercial advertising for the school in the community
options.B: Elimination of all school fees for enrolled students
options.C: Direct control over local government tax policies
options.D: Quick access to public health support during disease outbreaks

explanation: Spot on! Strong community ties mean the school won't have to face sudden health emergencies or disease outbreaks all on its own.

question: How does the endocrine system compare to the nervous system when it comes to response time?

options.A: It relies exclusively on electrical nerve impulses
options.B: It produces slower, longer-lasting responses
options.C: It produces faster, short-lived responses
options.D: It only functions during times of acute physical trauma

explanation: While the nervous system acts like a quick text message (fast and brief), the endocrine system acts more like a long letter—it takes a bit longer to arrive, but the effect sticks around much longer!

question: Why is checking on the emotional wellbeing of a patient in long-term traction a key part of your nursing care?

options.A: Anxious patients always disconnect their own traction
options.B: Good mental support replaces the need for pain meds
options.C: Stress stops bones from absorbing calcium
options.D: Being stuck in one position for weeks often brings down their mood and causes stress

explanation: Brilliant insight! Lying still for weeks takes a heavy emotional toll. Being a warm, listening ear is just as important as managing their physical injuries.

question: During a heart cell's action potential, which ion movement creates the long plateau phase?

options.A: Potassium entering the cell
options.B: Chloride leaving the cell
options.C: Sodium leaving the cell
options.D: Calcium entering the cell

explanation: As potassium tries to leave, a steady influx of calcium steps in to balance the electrical charge, creating a nice, steady plateau.

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping fast and calls the doctor using SBAR. What should go into the 'Recommendation' part?

options.A: Asking the doctor to come evaluate the patient or adjust medications
options.B: Listing the patient's full name, age, and home address in the ward
options.C: Describing the nursing school the nurse graduated from last year
options.D: Explaining the weather conditions outside the hospital building

explanation: Brilliant! The recommendation is your professional suggestion on what the team needs to do right now for the patient.

question: How many unique patient identifiers must a nurse check before giving any medication?

options.A: Zero identifiers
options.B: Two identifiers
options.C: One identifier
options.D: Four identifiers

explanation: Checking two unique identifiers, such as the patient's full name and hospital number, ensures the medicine goes to the right person. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h5)

question: During antenatal care for a multiple pregnancy, what should be a key focus of your nursing care?

options.A: Monitoring for early signs of preterm labor
options.B: Encouraging complete bed rest for all nine months
options.C: Stopping all routine ultrasound evaluations
options.D: Recommending a low-calorie diet to limit weight gain

explanation: Correct! Teaching mums to spot early tightenings or pressure, and making sure they keep their clinic visits, are top priorities to catch preterm labor early.

question: Which of these is an example of a capital budget expense in a hospital?

options.A: Buying disposable syringes for the emergency ward
options.B: Purchasing a brand-new CT scanner
options.C: Paying the monthly electricity bill for the pharmacy
options.D: Covering the weekly wages of ward support staff

explanation: Think of capital budgets as the big fund for expensive, long-lasting equipment and heavy machinery like a CT scanner, rather than daily supplies.

question: What exactly is a vesicovaginal fistula (VVF)?

options.A: An abnormal opening between the bladder and the vagina
options.B: A blockage in the tube carrying urine from the kidney
options.C: A complete failure of the kidneys to produce urine
options.D: An infection of the lining inside the urinary bladder

explanation: You nailed it! A VVF creates an unwanted channel between these two organs, which is why urine leaks through continuously. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: How does a hormonal IUD prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By thickening the cervical mucus to block sperm from entering
options.B: By making the vagina super acidic to destroy sperm on contact
options.C: By tricking the ovaries into releasing multiple eggs
options.D: By creating physical pressure that crushes any fertilized egg

explanation: The tiny bit of hormone released thickens the mucus at the cervix like a strong security guard—sperm just can't swim through it!

question: Which of these is a key behavioral warning sign that a school-aged child might be at risk?

options.A: Sudden and unexplained drop in academic performance
options.B: Consistent completion of all assigned homework tasks
options.C: Increased enthusiasm for structured extracurricular sports
options.D: Active participation in school health club meetings

explanation: Well done! A sudden, unexplained crash in grades usually means a child is dealing with hidden stress, abuse, or negative peer pressure.

question: Why is it important to match your physical assessment clues with lab hormone test results?

options.A: To replace the need for physician physical examinations
options.B: To calculate the exact date the disease started
options.C: To confirm diagnoses and evaluate treatment effectiveness
options.D: To eliminate the need for ongoing vital sign monitoring

explanation: Lab numbers tell one part of the story, and what you see with your own eyes tells the rest. Putting them together helps you see if the treatment plan is actually working.

question: Which of these is NOT a non-motor function linked to the cerebellum?

options.A: Language and word retrieval
options.B: Emotional mood modulation
options.C: Primary visual perception
options.D: Working memory and planning

explanation: Primary vision is handled in the occipital lobe at the back of the brain, not the cerebellum (though the cerebellum helps track eye movements!). You're crushing these questions.

question: You are assessing a patient with a newly created AV fistula in their arm. What finding tells you it is open and working well?

options.A: A palpable thrill and audible bruit over the fistula site
options.B: Absence of any sound or vibration when listening with a stethoscope
options.C: A cool hand with weak pulses past the surgical site
options.D: A strong pulse with severe pain and redness in the fingers

explanation: You'll love listening for this in the ward! When arterial and venous blood rush together, it creates a gentle vibration (thrill) and a swishing sound (bruit) that confirms good blood flow.

question: According to cell theory, where do all new cells come from?

options.A: Spontaneous generation
options.B: Extracellular fluid
options.C: Nutrients in the blood
options.D: Pre-existing cells

explanation: Cell theory states that life is continuous because all new cells are formed by the division of older, pre-existing cells. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary reason for keeping completed research questionnaires in a locked cabinet?

options.A: To ensure the forms do not get misplaced by staff
options.B: To make sure nobody steals the paper pens
options.C: To protect patient confidentiality and privacy
options.D: To comply with hospital interior design rules

explanation: Securing completed research documents is an ethical duty to protect participants' private health information. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h8)

question: Why must nurses monitor clients with neurological problems so closely?

options.A: Hospital insurance policies require hourly doctor visits
options.B: Small changes in condition can rapidly lead to major health crises
options.C: Clients with brain injuries usually refuse all oral medications
options.D: Nervous system tissues heal completely within a few hours

explanation: Because the central nervous system controls vital functions, even tiny changes in behavior or alertness can signal a dangerous decline. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h1)

question: How do unpredictable weather events directly impact food supply costs?

options.A: By destroying harvests, which reduces supply and drives up production expenses
options.B: By increasing the availability of cheap chemical fertilizers
options.C: By lowering the general cost of running heavy farm machinery
options.D: By stabilizing farmworker wages across different agricultural regions

explanation: Natural disasters and bad weather ruin crops, making available food scarcer and more expensive to produce. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h2)

question: What is the name of the temperature range known as the 'Danger Zone' where bacteria multiply super fast?

options.A: 0°C to 10°C
options.B: 5°C to 60°C
options.C: Minus 10°C to 0°C

explanation: Remember: 5°C to 60°C is the sweet spot for bacteria to throw a party and multiply rapidly. Keep hot foods hot and cold foods cold!

question: In SOAP charting, what kind of details go into the 'O' (Objective) section?

options.A: The patient's personal feelings and complaints
options.B: The nurse's personal opinion about the diagnosis
options.C: Measurable data like vital signs and lab results
options.D: The future medical orders written by the doctor

explanation: Correct! Objective data means facts you can measure, see, or test, like blood pressure and lab values.

question: What role do cultural traditions play in nutrition?

options.A: They ensure that every person eats a balanced amount of vitamins
options.B: They prevent communities from consuming processed fast foods
options.C: They dictate the exact financial cost of groceries in a market
options.D: They dictate what foods are considered acceptable and how meals are prepared

explanation: Culture shapes food preferences, cooking methods, and the social significance attached to eating together. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h5)

question: At 34 weeks, an antenatal patient is found to have a soft heart murmur. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Immediately send the patient to the emergency operating theatre
options.B: Recognize it as a common normal finding due to increased blood volume
options.C: Order emergency blood transfusions to correct severe anemia
options.D: Diagnose the patient with permanent rheumatic heart disease

explanation: Brilliant! Extra blood flow and heart position changes often cause harmless murmurs during pregnancy. No need to panic!

question: What makes communication in home health care different from a hospital setting?

options.A: Communication is restricted by hospital rules
options.B: Nurses rely solely on written medical charts
options.C: The nurse enters a private home as a guest
options.D: Patients have no family members present

explanation: Stepping into a patient's personal space completely changes the dynamic! Unlike a controlled clinic, you are a guest in their domain, which calls for extra respect and adaptability.

question: How do you calculate the mean (average) of a set of numbers?

options.A: Find the exact middle number after sorting values from lowest to highest
options.B: Add all values together and divide by the total number of values
options.C: Subtract the lowest number from the highest number in the group
options.D: Identify the single value that appears most frequently in the data set

explanation: The mean is simply your standard arithmetic average! Just add up all your observations and divide by how many there are.

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle used to study diseases?

options.A: Agent, host, and environment
options.B: Patient, nurse, and doctor
options.C: Bacteria, vaccine, and immunity
options.D: Clinic, hospital, and laboratory

explanation: Always remember the trio: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (where they meet). Simple and classic nursing knowledge!

question: A patient has swollen ankles. How should you advise them to position their legs when resting?

options.A: Dangling freely off the edge of the bed
options.B: Crossed tightly at the knees for stability
options.C: Flat on the floor while sitting in a chair
options.D: Elevated above the level of the heart

explanation: You've got this! Gravity is our helper here. Raising the legs higher than the heart lets trapped fluid flow smoothly back into circulation.

question: A patient is discouraged because their BMI hasn't budged after starting an exercise routine. What else can you suggest tracking?

options.A: Waist circumference and overall energy levels
options.B: Resting body temperature and pulse rate
options.C: Daily fluid retention and shoe size changes
options.D: Total body height measured twice a week

explanation: Spot on! When starting fitness, patients often swap fat for muscle. Checking waist size and energy levels will often show great progress before the scale moves!

question: Besides antibodies, what specific viral marker do fourth-generation HIV tests look for?

options.A: p24 antigen
options.B: Integrase enzyme
options.C: Reverse transcriptase
options.D: gp120 protein

explanation: Awesome work! Fourth-gen tests search for the p24 antigen alongside antibodies, helping us catch recent infections much earlier.

question: Why might a doctor choose a transjejunal feeding tube instead of a standard gastric tube?

options.A: To bypass the stomach entirely due to high aspiration risk
options.B: To provide a larger reservoir for liquid formula storage
options.C: To make daily stoma site cleaning much easier for caregivers
options.D: To allow the patient to chew and swallow food while feeding

explanation: Transjejunal tubes deliver nutrients further down into the small bowel, which helps prevent severe reflux and aspiration in vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why must you split a 5ml medication dose into two separate injection sites for an adult?

options.A: Single adult IM sites should not exceed three milliliters
options.B: Thick oils prevent the plunger from moving past three milliliters
options.C: Patients are allergic to volumes greater than two milliliters
options.D: All syringes break if filled past the halfway mark

explanation: That's right! Putting more than 3ml into one muscle site causes too much pressure, severe pain, and poor drug absorption. Splitting it keeps your patient comfortable.

question: Experienced nurses are resigning in droves because they feel invisible and unsupported. What should management do first?

options.A: Stop holding staff meetings to prevent nurses from voicing complaints
options.B: Issue strict warning memos about the consequences of resigning early
options.C: Establish structured mentorship and recognition programs for clinical achievements
options.D: Reduce salaries across all departments to save money for recruitment ads

explanation: To stop nurses from leaving, you have to show them they matter! Recognizing their hard work and setting up supportive mentorship makes all the difference.

question: How do vaccines work to protect a child's body against infections?

options.A: By stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies
options.B: By coating the stomach lining to block germ absorption
options.C: By increasing the body temperature to kill viruses
options.D: By providing immediate chemical destruction of all bacteria

explanation: Exactly! Vaccines introduce safe, weakened parts of a germ to train the immune system so it knows how to fight back if the real disease ever shows up.

question: Which of these clinical variables is measured using a nominal scale?

options.A: Weight of an infant in kilograms
options.B: Patient admission diagnosis code
options.C: Body temperature in degrees Celsius
options.D: Pain score rated from zero to ten

explanation: Diagnosis codes are just labels used to group patient conditions. A malaria code isn't 'higher' than a typhoid code—they're just different categories.

question: What do we call the medical measurement of the inside of a woman's pelvis to check if she can deliver vaginally?

options.A: Hysteroscopy
options.B: Amniocentesis
options.C: Episiotomy
options.D: Pelvimetry

explanation: You've got this! Pelvimetry is just measuring the birth canal dimensions to make sure everything can fit safely.

question: What is a major problem when a hospital runs on a strictly punitive (blame-heavy) culture?

options.A: Errors are driven underground out of fear of punishment
options.B: Clinical outcomes improve because mistakes stop happening
options.C: Employee innovation and creativity increase significantly
options.D: Staff members report mistakes immediately and openly

explanation: If staff know they will be heavily punished for minor mistakes, they will hide them instead of reporting them. This stops the team from learning and keeps patients unsafe!

question: Which tool is most commonly used for rapid neurological assessment in emergency settings?

options.A: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.B: Comprehensive mental status questionnaire
